page: Amazon Web Services r8in.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server based on the x86_64 architecture. The host is configured with 192 dedicated physical Intel cores running two threads per core, yielding 384 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. System memory totals 3072.0 GB, which aligns with an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 600 Gbps, enabling high-volume network transfers for distributed data pipelines. The system contains no integrated local NVMe storage, requiring input and output operations to rely entirely on network-attached storage such as Amazon Elastic Block Store. No discrete GPUs or hardware accelerators are provisioned on this instance.

Direct bare-metal access removes hypervisor overhead, providing uninterrupted access to memory subsystems and physical CPU execution units. This resource profile matches large-scale memory-resident applications, distributed caching tiers, enterprise relational databases, and in-memory analytics platforms that require dense memory pools alongside significant network bandwidth.

These specifications align directly with large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, big data analytics engines, and large-scale data caching infrastructures.
